stance_summary: Fade the post-FOMC US front-end overshoot: US 2Y has packed a 1-month +57bp / ~3.3σ cheapening into a hike that was already >90% priced, leaving 4.76% ~76-101bp above the new 3.75-4.00% funds band while US temperature gauges sit near 50. That is a move-stretch with a delivered-event reversal condition, not a 5y valuation short. Receive US 2Y rather than fade AUDNZD, whose 5y z is larger but cannot be anchored to NZ yields in this packet.

expression_comparison.rates_candidate: Receive/long US_2Y at executable_marks.rates.US_2Y 4.76 (market_state.rates.US.tenors.2Y.value as of 2026-09-18). Fade the 1M +57bp / z 3.29 cheapening and 1y 99.8th percentile print after a delivered, >90% priced 25bp hike, using the 3.75-4.00% funds band as the policy-rate anchor.
expression_comparison.spot_candidate: Short AUDNZD at executable_marks.spot_fx.AUDNZD 1.246846846846847 (market_state.fx.pairs.AUDNZD.spot as of 2026-09-18). 1y percentile 99.80 / 5y percentile 99.96 / z_5y 3.12 with 1m +4.27%, against AU housing (NSW stamp duty -24% y/y, volumes -18%, Sydney/Melbourne values >7% off peak) and a NZ Q2 GDP 0.2% q/q beat.
expression_comparison.rationale: Rates are selected because the discrepancy being faded is the US front-end MOVE overshoot after a priced FOMC hike, which lives in US 2Y, has a frozen executable mark, and has a policy-rate anchor (funds 3.75-4.00 vs 2Y 4.76). AUDNZD is the cleaner 5y LEVEL stretch (z_5y 3.12 vs US 2Y z_5y only 0.89) but is inferior here: NZ sovereign yields are unavailable so the cross cannot be risk-matched to a rate differential; AUDUSD is not analogously stretched (z_5y 1.23, 1m +0.20%); and 1d AUDNZD is still +0.65% with no completed reversal print. When the identified mispricing is a US rates overshoot and both expressions are otherwise usable, the rates-first default holds.

trade.structure: Outright receive US 2Y duration. Paper side long so the books engine's inverted yield P&L profits if the marked yield falls from 4.76.
trade.thesis: FACT: On 2026-09-16 the Fed raised 25bp to 3.75-4.00%; futures had entered that decision with >90% odds of the hike. FACT: US 2Y is 4.76 as of 2026-09-18 (executable_marks.rates.US_2Y / market_state.rates.US.tenors.2Y.value), 1y percentile 99.80, z_1y 2.84, 5y percentile 88.0, z_5y 0.89, with bp_1d +9.0 (screen 1D z 1.90), bp_1m +57.0 (screen 1M z 3.29), bp_5d +13.0. FACT: US 5s10s is 15.0bp, z_1y -2.77 / 5y z +0.07; US 2s10s is 25.0bp, 1y percentile 0.20, z_1y -2.45 / 5y z +0.33 — the flatten is a 1y-window symptom of the same front-end cheapening, not a 5y curve extreme. FACT: US temperature gauges are Inflation 52.0 (core PCE +0.2% m/m, ~2.4% 1m/3m ann., ~3.0% 6m), Labor 50.2, Activity 49.92, Consumer 48.5. FACT: VIX 15.44 (14.7th percentile) and SPX 7637.76 (90.1st) are not a stress regime. INFERENCE: The 1-month 3.3σ US 2Y cheapening is crowded extrapolation of already-known CPI-plus-hike information; known information needs a new transmission mechanism to justify another 9bp cheapening two sessions after the decision. The economically relevant anchor is the policy rate, not the 5y yield percentile: 4.76 sits ~76-101bp above the new funds band after a single 25bp step. Receiving 2Y owns that overshoot; a 5s10s steepener would only own the relative symptom and is a 1y-only extreme. UNKNOWN: whether additional hikes remain in the (unobserved here) SEP path; CME FX positioning is unavailable; 1y screen n=252 is not a full-cycle distribution. Do not treat 4.76 as a 5y statistical blow-off (z_5y 0.89).
trade.mispricing: US 2Y prices roughly 76-101bp of extra tightening above the just-set 3.75-4.00% funds band after a hike that was already >90% priced, and has just printed a 1-month +57bp / z 3.29 cheapening. That gap is the overshoot. The 5y z of 0.89 is explicit null-as-extreme: this is not a secular richness claim.
why_now: The Sep 16 hike has already printed and was >90% priced into the decision; residual +9bp on Sep 18 is post-event extrapolation, not new information.
US 2Y 1M +57bp at screen z 3.29 is the sharpest rates MOVE stretch in the frozen screens; US temps near 50 do not corroborate a fresh tightening impulse.
Empty $100m seed book pays 5% ACT/365 on the full allocation whether flat or deployed; a 20-35bp giveback of the 57bp spike is the only path this seat has to outrun that clock.
evidence_refs: rollup:August CPI keeps the Fed tightening bias intact
rollup:Australian housing downturn deepens under higher rates
rollup:New Zealand Q2 GDP slows to 0.2% q/q but beats forecasts
rollup:BoC minutes flag higher energy pass-through risk
trade.horizon: 2-6 weeks (post-hike digestion of the 1-month front-end overshoot)
trade.invalidation: Thesis is wrong if a new hawkish transmission arrives after the already-delivered hike: another upside US inflation surprise that re-opens additional hike odds, or US 2Y continuing to cheapen to fresh 1y extremes without a giveback of the 1-month +57bp spike. Right-thesis/wrong-timing if yields chop around 4.76 while the funds-to-2Y gap stays wide; reassess horizon rather than invent a stop. 5y z_5y 0.89 remaining mid-range is not itself invalidation.
catalysts: Post-FOMC digestion: fade of residual hike/CPI extrapolation now that the 25bp step is delivered.
US data that fails to validate further tightening beyond temps already near 50.
AU housing downturn as independent evidence that tightening channels bite, supporting a broader front-end giveback without being the traded expression.
principal_risks: Retained 'August CPI keeps the Fed tightening bias intact' can extend the cheapening if the hike is the start of a sequence rather than the overshoot.
Energy-market shock absorbers weakening and BoC energy pass-through are upside-yield risks that can leak into US 2Y.
US 2Y 5y percentile is only 88.0 / z 0.89 — a higher-for-longer regime can keep 4.76 as a new normal.
CME FX positioning is unavailable; ownership of the 2Y cheapening is not independently triangulated from futures positioning in allowed evidence_refs.
Paper P&L on percent-quoted yields is small per bp even at $80m, so a slow giveback can lose to the 5% ACT/365 clock.

remit: fade statistically or fundamentally stretched market moves when reversal conditions exist

conflict_synopsis.core_view: Receive US 2Y to fade a 1-month +57bp / ~3.3σ post-hike front-end overshoot versus a 3.75-4.00% funds anchor, not a 5y valuation short.
conflict_synopsis.key_catalyst: Delivered Sep 16 25bp hike that was already >90% priced, with residual +9bp cheapening on Sep 18.
conflict_synopsis.key_invalidation: New hawkish US inflation/policy transmission that re-opens additional hikes, or US 2Y making fresh 1y extremes without giving back the 1-month spike.

paper_capital.funding_hurdle_rationale: The seat pays 5.00% ACT/365 on the full $100m every day whether flat or deployed (~$13.7k/day). Being flat has zero expected trading P&L against that vig. Long US_2Y at the frozen 4.76 mark: books P&L is inverted yield, so a 25bp giveback on $80m is 0.25/100*80m=$200k (~15 days of funding) and a 35bp giveback is $280k (~20 days). The 1-month +57bp / z 3.29 cheapening after a priced hike is large enough that a partial mean-reversion inside 2-6 weeks can clear the clock; $80m is sized up because percent-quoted 2Y P&L per bp is small. Carry of receiving 4.76 versus the 3.75-4.00% funds band supports the position while waiting. If the 5y z of 0.89 is the true regime and yields do not give back, the trade fails the hurdle and is invalidated by a fresh hawkish print rather than by sitting flat.
